summary: @nebula.js/snapshooter 0.6.1 ships preinstall alternate-runtime dropper executing obfuscated payload under Bun
details: The package's `preinstall` script runs `node setup.mjs`, which downloads the Bun runtime from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/` to a temp directory, chmod +x's the binary, and `execFileSync`s it against a sibling `math_init.js` at `npm install` time. `math_init.js` is a 727KB Bun-compiled bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header) processed with obfuscator.io transforms (hex-named identifiers, shuffled string-array with a rotator, large numeric constant table). The file is not declared in `package.json`'s `files` array (which lists only `client.js` and `server.js`) yet ships in the published tarball. The package is published under the `@nebula.js` scope attributed to QlikTech International AB / qlik-oss/nebula.js, whose legitimate snapshooter is a small Puppeteer wrapper with no preinstall hook, no `setup.mjs`, and no `math_init.js` — this version adds the dropper on top of the original code, consistent with a trojanized release under a reputable scope. Executing an undeclared obfuscated payload under a freshly downloaded alien interpreter at install time gives the publisher arbitrary code execution on every installer's machine and is designed to evade Node-based static scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
